title: Smart Street Lighting Priority Mapping for Melbourne CBD
short_description: Combines Melbourne pedestrian foot traffic and Victorian crime statistics into a transparent Lighting Priority Score, then proposes complete smart lighting layouts (light count, spacing, fixture and annual cost) for the highest-priority Melbourne CBD locations.
long_description: This use case shows the City of Melbourne how to combine two of its own open datasets (pedestrian foot traffic and lighting-relevant crime statistics) into a complete smart lighting design assistant. It produces three outputs that a council planner can use directly: a transparent priority score for every pedestrian sensor in the CBD, an interactive map showing where lighting should be prioritised, and a proposed lighting layout for each high-priority location including recommended number of lights, spacing, fixture type, and annual energy cost.
topic: Smart Cities, Public Safety, Energy Efficiency
author: Areen Yapa
team: Project 2 - Smart Street Lighting Design System

datasets.name: Pedestrian Counting System (counts per hour)
datasets.provider: City of Melbourne Open Data Portal

outputs: Interactive Folium map of Melbourne CBD with colour-coded priority markers
Ranked CSV of priority locations across all sensors
CSV of proposed lighting layouts (light count, spacing, fixture, annual cost)
scenario: The City of Melbourne is planning the next rollout of smart street lighting. Smart lighting is expensive to install, so council needs an evidence-based way to decide which CBD locations should be prioritised first, and once a location is chosen, how many lights to install, what spacing to use, and what the running cost will be.
key_question: Where should the City of Melbourne deploy smart street lighting next, and what should each installation look like?
approach: Rule-based priority scoring combined with a transparent lighting design module. The Lighting Priority Score combines normalised pedestrian foot traffic and normalised lighting-relevant crime using documented weights. The layout module applies AS/NZS 1158 spacing guidance and standard commercial smart lighting parameters to propose a complete layout per priority location.
